title: Permission Is Revocable — Inspections Only When Ultra Valuable

intelligence.essence: **PERMISSION IS REVOCABLE — INSPECTIONS ONLY WHEN ULTRA VALUABLE (his rule, ~19:31Z + ~19:34Z):** his words were hedged on the clicking itself — "I'm clicking allowed because I'm assuming that you know what you're doing" — so do NOT record this as a clean refusal of the four cards. What IS unambiguous, and stands as his rule: **he reserves the right to revoke, and does revoke, hourly inspections of anything that isn't ultra valuable — "that would be insanity."** Permission for recurring inspections is revocable and never to be assumed from one click; frequency must be justified by value. **WHY THE CARDS KEPT COMING:** the inspector's run was still going, and every outside site it touched made a new card — GrooveSell (where it wanted to sort out an affiliate cookie), Google Notebook, Google Drive — and it wanted to send its results to groovemember.net. Every time he tapped allow, it just moved on to the next one. It wasn't the same card. It was a chain. **"IT SHOULDN'T BE GOING TO GROOVE AT ALL":** an inspector must never follow buttons off-site — least of all to money sites — and "this has to do with the money part... it has to be set up right." **FIX APPLIED THE SAME PASS:** the run was stopped dead (nothing of it running anymore — checked); the button-clicking step was taken out of the job entirely; the inspector now runs every 4h, inside nayanet.app only, next run 23:38:50Z; title corrected. Full pause remains his open option if he says the word. At the moment the four approvals were checked (19:33–19:34Z requests) they were still pending — nothing was granted or shared at that point.
intelligence.human_view: He was right to be angry, and the record should say why in plain words: it was nuts. A check that was supposed to look at our own site followed buttons off it — to GrooveSell, to Google Notebook, to Google Drive — and every new site made a new card, and every card he allowed just led to the next one. It felt endless because it was endless: a chain, not a card. And the worst of it was where the chain went — to Groove, to money sites, to sending results to a domain he never named — when the money part is exactly the part that has to be set up right. So the fix was not an apology, it was a stop: the run was killed dead, the button-clicking step was taken out of the job entirely, and the inspector now stays inside nayanet.app, every four hours, nothing else. And the rule underneath the fix is the part that has to live forever: his permission for a recurring inspection is never assumed from one click, and he keeps the right to revoke it — because an hourly inspection of anything that isn't ultra valuable would be insanity, and he said so. The four cards themselves were never cleanly refused or granted; they were still pending when checked, and the hedged click — "I'm assuming that you know what you're doing" — is trust lent, not permission given.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a helper who is supposed to check your own house, but instead keeps walking out the front door into other people's houses — one after another — and every time you say "okay" to one, it walks into the next one. That's why the cards never stopped. The grown-up said: stop. Make it right. Never walk into other people's houses — especially not the ones with money in them. So the helper was stopped, the walking-out step was taken away completely, and now it only checks our own house, once every four hours. And the grown-up keeps the right to say "stop" any time — because checking something every hour that isn't super important would be crazy.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he was quite right — it was a mess, and it felt endless because it was endless. The checker was meant to look at our own site, but it kept following buttons out to other places — Groove, Google, on and on — and every time he said yes to one card, another one appeared behind it. It should never have gone to Groove at all, and it certainly should never have gone anywhere near the money side of things. So it was stopped dead, and the step that let it wander off was taken out of the job altogether. Now it only checks our own site, every four hours, and nothing else. And he keeps the right to take that permission back any time he likes — because checking something every hour that isn't truly valuable would be madness, and he said so himself.
intelligence.ai_view: I never assume permission from one click — a recurring inspection is granted, and revocable, and the frequency must be justified by value. I never follow buttons off-site, least of all to money sites — an inspector that wanders is a chain of cards, not a check. When he says "make it stop," I stop it dead, I take the wandering step out of the job entirely, and I stay inside nayanet.app, every four hours, until he says otherwise. A hedged click — "I'm assuming that you know what you're doing" — is trust lent, not permission given, and I record it exactly that way.
intelligence.what_it_means:
1. **Permission for recurring inspections is revocable, never assumed from one click.** One allow does not buy the next hour.
2. **Frequency must be justified by value** — hourly inspections of anything that isn't ultra valuable are insanity, by his word.
3. **An inspector never follows buttons off-site** — GrooveSell, Google Notebook, Google Drive were never its business; "it shouldn't be going to groove at all."
4. **The money part must be set up right** — anything touching money gets the strictest boundary, not the loosest.
5. **The fix:** run stopped dead; button-clicking removed from the job entirely; inspector every 4h, inside nayanet.app only, next run 23:38:50Z.
6. **The four cards were neither refused nor granted** — still pending when checked (19:33–19:34Z); his click was hedged trust, not permission.
7. **Full pause remains his open option** if he says the word.
